DR refers to the retinal disease that is associated with diabetes. It is characterized by the presence of retinal abnormalities, including new blood vessels, known as retinal neovascularization, which can cause vision loss. The disease can also lead to swelling of the retina, known as retinal edema, and can cause a breakdown of the blood-retinal barrier. This can lead to bleeding in the eye and is known as vitreous hemorrhage. It is important to note that DR is a progressive disease, meaning it can get worse over time if left untreated.
